Trump’s Fixation on Arctic Ships Led to Billions in No-Bid Contracts

Earlier this year, my colleagues and I set out to solve a puzzle: Why is the Trump administration awarding contracts for Arctic vessels from Finland, sidestepping the usual rules designed to protect taxpayer money?
Trump’s fascination with icebreakers can be traced to a chance encounter in Helsinki more than 30 years ago, when the future president was on a business trip.
Fast forward to March 2025, when Trump won a golf tournament alongside Alexander Stubb, the president of Finland. Afterward, Trump announced an agreement to buy icebreakers.
That deal eventually grew to be 11 icebreakers, twice as many as the Coast Guard previously said it needed. And those vessels come at a high cost. The contracts are worth almost $7 billion.
The deal reveals how the Trump administration often operates: ignoring the norms around government spending, in pursuit of projects that reflect the president’s desires.
